raw.questionText: Let $A$ be the $3 \times 3$ real symmetric matrix $A = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 2 & 1 \\ 2 & 5 & 2 \\ 1 & 2 & 3 \end{pmatrix}$ and let $B$ be any non-zero $3 \times 3$ real skew-symmetric matrix such that the matrix $A+B$ is invertible. If $C = (A+B)^{-1}(A-B)$, find the value of $\det( C^T (A+B) C + A - B )$.
raw.explanation: Using the transpose properties of symmetric and skew-symmetric matrices, we show that $C^T(A+B)C = A+B$, simplifying the expression inside the determinant to $2A$.
raw._insight: Using the transpose properties of symmetric and skew-symmetric matrices, we show that $C^T(A+B)C = A+B$, simplifying the expression inside the determinant to $2A$.
